plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price is determined by my own sealed bid. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy—if I bid higher than my value, I risk paying more than the item is worth; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $28, I should bid exactly $28 to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my bid only determines when I exit the clock. In second-price auctions, bidding my true value is a dominant strategy - if I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying above my value; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $23.

Since the auction mechanism results in the winner paying the second-highest bid (like a second-price auction), bidding my true value is the weakly dominant strategy.
